summary: This note covers the immediate aftermath of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster, focusing on President Ronald Reagan's response. Reagan postponed his scheduled State of the Union address by a week and instead gave a national address from the Oval Office. The speech was written by Peggy Noonan and is described as one of the most significant speeches of the 20th century by a survey of 137 communication scholars.
one_line: Reagan's national address from the Oval Office after the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster, written by Peggy Noonan.
key_facts: President Ronald Reagan had been scheduled to give his annual State of the Union address on the night of the Challenger disaster.
Reagan initially announced that the State of the Union address would go on as scheduled.
Reagan later postponed the State of the Union address for a week.
Reagan instead gave a national address on the Challenger disaster from the Oval Office of the White House.
The Challenger disaster national address was written by Peggy Noonan.
A survey of 137 communication scholars listed the Challenger address as one of the most significant speeches of the 20th century.
The address finished with a statement that quoted from the poem "High Flight".
"High Flight" was written by John Gillespie Magee, Jr.
